title: Amazon EventBridge custom event bus to AWS Lambda with AWS Glue Schema Registry Avro
description: Publish an Avro event to an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus, decoded against an AWS Glue Schema Registry, and deliver it as JSON to AWS Lambda

introBox.headline: How it works
text: This pattern shows how to publish a rich domain event, Avro-encoded, to an Amazon EventBridge custom event bus (the eventsv2 API) using PutRawEvents together with an AWS Glue Schema Registry, and then deliver that same event to an AWS Lambda subscriber.

The publisher encodes an OrderPlaced event against an Avro schema and wraps it in the Glue wire format. EventBridge decodes the Avro against the Glue registry server-side and delivers the payload as plain JSON, so the consumer Lambda needs no Avro library and simply logs the event to Amazon CloudWatch. A matching orderId, fields, and metadata prove the delivered event equals the one that was published.
This deploys one EventBridge custom event bus, one subscriber, an AWS Glue Schema Registry and Avro schema, one Python 3.14 Lambda function, an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue, and the delivery role.
Install the publisher dependencies: python3 -m venv .venv && ./.venv/bin/pip install -r publisher/requirements.txt
Publish one Avro OrderPlaced event: scripts/run_publish.sh <stack-name> <region>
View the delivered event: aws logs tail /aws/lambda/avro-orders-consumer --since 5m --format short
See the GitHub repo for detailed testing instructions.
Confirm the stack has been deleted: aws cloudformation list-stacks --query "StackSummaries[?contains(StackName,'STACK_NAME')].StackStatus"
